title: Norm coefficient projection on supported rationalized lattice generators
statement:
Fix distinct primes $p,\ell$, a separably closed field $K$ of characteristic $p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ inside an algebraic closure $\Omega$, and the extended norm topology on $E,\Omega$. Let $\mathcal O_E=\{x\in E:|x|\leq1\}$ with its subspace topology [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. On profinite sets put $A(P)=C(P,E)$, $O(P)=C(P,\mathcal O_E)$ and $B(P)=C(P,\Omega)$, using all continuous functions, and let $A\to B$ be inclusion [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring]. For a scheme $Y$ put $R_Y=p_Y^*R$ for $R=O,A,B$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. Use internal module objects, ordinary unbounded derived categories and K-flat derived tensor [sk-def-sfb-module-objects, sk-def-sfb-derived-categories, sk-def-sfb-derived-tensor-hom].

Let $T$ be separated of finite type over $K$, let $a:S\hookrightarrow T$ be a constructible locally closed immersion, and let $L_0$ be a lisse finite-rank $O_S$-module [def-sfb-lisse-coefficient-module]. Factor $a=i\circ j$ as an open immersion into its closure followed by the closed immersion and put $a_!=i_*j_!$ using the exact coefficient-module functors [lem-weil-pbc-condensed-open-closed-recollement]. Put $Q=A_T\otimes_{O_T}a_!L_0$, as a complex in degree zero. Let $\mathcal H_R=Rp_{T*,R}$ be the ordinary right derived direct image of module sheaves from $T_{\mathrm{proet}}$ to internal condensed $R$-modules, for $R=A,B$ [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull, sk-def-sfb-pullback-from-point]. Then the specified morphism
$$\pi_Q:B\otimes_A^L\mathcal H_A(Q)\longrightarrow\mathcal H_B(B_T\otimes_{A_T}^LQ)$$
is an isomorphism in $D(\operatorname{Mod}_B)$. It is the adjoint, under derived scalar extension and restriction, of $\mathcal H_A(Q)\to\mathcal H_A(\operatorname{Res}(B_T\otimes^L_{A_T}Q))\cong\operatorname{Res}\mathcal H_B(B_T\otimes^L_{A_T}Q)$ induced by $q\mapsto1\otimes q$ on a flat-term K-flat resolution. Equivalently it is the counit-adjoint coefficient projection for $p_T$. Empty $S,T$ and $L_0=0$ are included. No completeness of $\Omega$, flatness of $A\to B$, finite-subextension-valued replacement of $B$, assertion about arbitrary constructible complexes, or arithmetic Galois-action comparison is assumed.

proof.text: All schemes in the argument are separated of finite type over the given field, hence Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. By [det-prop-sfb-qlbar-colimit-x-invert-ell], $A_Y=O_Y[1/\ell]$ is flat over $O_Y$. Put $L=A_S\otimes_{O_S}L_0$. Locally where $L_0=O_S^r$, this is $A_S^r$ in degree zero, including $r=0$. The open and closed tensor projection isomorphisms [lem-sfb-condensed-support-projection-formula] identify the actual $Q$ with $a_!L[0]$, not just their restrictions to $S$. The unit-normalized inverse-image/tensor maps are those of [lem-sfb-kflat-scalar-comparison-normalization]. Thus [lem-sfb-coefficient-heart-lisse-extension-constructible] makes $Q$ bounded constructible over $A_T$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent proof of geometric norm-coefficient projection, using independent proper finiteness and tame-boundary inputs.

proof.text: For every scheme $Z$ in this setting write $T_Z=B_Z\otimes^L_{A_Z}-$ and denote the counit-adjoint coefficient projection for $h:X\to Y$ by $\beta_{h,K}$. Scalar extension takes every bounded constructible $A_Z$-complex to a bounded constructible $B_Z$-complex. Indeed [det-cor-coefficient-heart-ii-generation] gives a finite cone-and-shift construction from $c_!N$ with $N$ finite-rank lisse over $A$. On a trivializing cover $T_SN=B_S^r[0]$; no flatness of $A\to B$ is used. The support tensor isomorphisms identify $T_Zc_!N$ with $c_!T_SN$. These are generators of the triangulated category in [lem-sfb-continuous-qbar-constructible-generators], so the finite construction remains bounded constructible. By [det-sf-comp-continuous-algcl-constructible-tor] it has finite Tor amplitude. The same finite-local-model reasoning applies to $T_Y$ of any bounded constructible output over $A$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent proof of geometric norm-coefficient projection, using independent proper finiteness and tame-boundary inputs.

proof.text: First establish $\beta_{h,K}$ for an arbitrary proper $h:X\to Y$ in the setting and bounded constructible $A_X$-complex $K$. By [det-thm-sfb-proper-base-change-rational](2), $Rh_{*,A}K$ is bounded constructible. By step 2 and [det-sf-comp-continuous-algcl-finiteness], every cohomology sheaf of $Rh_{*,B}T_XK$ has finite constant local models on a constructible stratification. Only this cohomological constructibility is needed here, not a uniform upper bound. For every geometric $y$, [lem-sfb-constructible-normed-geometric-fibres] therefore makes the degree-$q$ fibre of this target a finite-dimensional $\Omega$-vector space, for each $q$. Its source has bounded constructible cohomology by step 2. The recorded finiteness theorem's representative $\operatorname{PadicAlgCl}(\ell)$ can be replaced by $\Omega$: choose the algebraic-closure isomorphism of [lem-pc-algebraic-closure-exists-unique]. It is isometric on each finite subextension by [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-absolute-value], hence on the algebraic union. It induces isomorphic continuous-function rings; [lem-sfb-condensed-coefficient-iso-constructible] preserves the finite-Tor constructible input, and the induced exact module equivalences identify the underlying direct images and their cohomology.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent proof of geometric norm-coefficient projection, using independent proper finiteness and tame-boundary inputs.

proof.text: The inclusion $A\to B$ need not be flat. Nevertheless scalar restriction commutes with these derived direct images: the two functors $\operatorname{Res}_Y Rh_{*,B}$ and $Rh_{*,A}\operatorname{Res}_X$ are right adjoints of the canonically isomorphic left functors $h_B^*T_Y$ and $T_Xh_A^*$. The scalar adjunction is [lem-pur-sheaf-ring-derived-coefficient-adjunction] and the left-functor comparison is [lem-sfb-kflat-scalar-comparison-normalization]. Their Hom adjunctions give a natural bijection for every test object and hence the unique comparison isomorphism, preserving the adjunction units. Consequently the transpose defining $\beta$ is the direct image of the insertion $K\to\operatorname{Res}T_XK$, with insertion $k\mapsto1\otimes k$ on a flat-term K-flat representative. This argument does not invoke the flat-only underived-restriction lemmas.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent proof of geometric norm-coefficient projection, using independent proper finiteness and tame-boundary inputs.

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-algcl-countable-closed-finite-cover], $\Omega$ has at most countable algebraic dimension over $E$. Apply [lem-sfb-countable-normed-orthogonal-basis] to $V=\Omega$ with prescribed $b_0=1$. Write $D=\operatorname{End}^{\mathrm{cts}}_E(\Omega)$, $\lambda_0$ for its first coordinate and $e(v)=\lambda_0(v)1$. Each $d\in D$ induces an $A$-linear endomorphism of $B$ by postcomposition on every profinite test, and hence of $B_X$ and $T_XK$ after forgetting $B$-linearity. These maps preserve composition and addition. Also $eB$ is the actual copy of $A$; its inclusion and retraction are induced by $E\hookrightarrow\Omega$ and $\lambda_0$, with composite the identity. Tensoring, derived direct image and the exact fibre functor preserve this split summand. The underlying derived tensor and the scalar adjunction use the same flat-term representative [lem-sfb-internal-section-scalar-adjunction].

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent proof of geometric norm-coefficient projection, using independent proper finiteness and tame-boundary inputs.

proof.text: Fix $y,q$ and put $H=H^q\Phi_{y,A}(Rh_{*,A}\operatorname{Res}T_XK)$. Step 4 and the fibre/restriction compatibility identify it with the underlying $E$-space of $H^q\Phi_{y,B}(Rh_{*,B}T_XK)$. It is a unital $D$-module by step 5. Its $E$-dimension is at most countable: by step 3 it is finite-dimensional over $\Omega$, which is countable-dimensional over $E$. The split idempotent identifies $eH$ with $H^q\Phi_{y,A}(Rh_{*,A}K)$. Apply [lem-sfb-countable-endomorphism-module-reconstruction]. Its isomorphism is $v\otimes h\mapsto\theta_vh$, where $\theta_v(w)=\lambda_0(w)v$. Since $b_0=1$, $\theta_v=m_v e$, with $m_v$ multiplication by $v\in\Omega$. It follows that this is exactly $v\otimes h\mapsto v\,H^q\Phi_y(Rh_*(\eta_K))(h)$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent proof of geometric norm-coefficient projection, using independent proper finiteness and tame-boundary inputs.

proof.text: The derived scalar/fibre comparison in [lem-sfb-constructible-normed-geometric-fibres] identifies the degree-$q$ geometric fibre of the source of $\beta$ with $\Omega\otimes_E H^q\Phi_{y,A}(Rh_{*,A}K)$: scalar tensor over the abstract field $E$ is exact. By the insertion-of-one normalization in step 4 its map to the target is precisely the isomorphism in step 6. Thus all cohomology-fibre maps are invertible. Conservativity on bounded constructible complexes applies after truncating the target to any finite interval containing the source's cohomology: its cohomology in every other degree has all fibres zero, so is zero by the degree-zero constructible detection assertion of [lem-sfb-constructible-normed-geometric-fibres]. Both objects are therefore bounded constructible, and the same assertion proves $\beta_{h,K}$ invertible. This proves the proper comparison without a base-change assertion for $B$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent proof of geometric norm-coefficient projection, using independent proper finiteness and tame-boundary inputs.

proof.text: For a quasi-compact open $j:U\hookrightarrow X$, consider bounded constructible $C$ over $A_U$ for which $\beta_{j,C}$ is invertible. The two functors defining $\beta$ are exact and its transformation commutes with shifts by [lem-sfb-ringed-projection-first-shift]; [lem-sf-triangle-two-out-of-three] makes this class closed under cones and shifts. It is also closed under finite sums and retracts. Explicitly, if $C\xrightarrow{i}H\xrightarrow{r}C$ has $ri=1$ and $\beta_H$ is invertible, then $F(r)\beta_H^{-1}G(i)$ is the inverse of $\beta_C$ by the two naturality squares, where $F=T_XRj_{*,A}$ and $G=Rj_{*,B}T_U$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent proof of geometric norm-coefficient projection, using independent proper finiteness and tame-boundary inputs.

proof.text: Use [lem-sfb-tame-pair-proper-generators] for this $j$. A generator is $G=Rq_{*,A}K$, with $p:Y\to X$ proper, $V=p^{-1}U$, $q:V\to U$ proper, $j':V\hookrightarrow Y$, and $K=b_!L[0]$ for the stated tame normal-crossings pair. Here $K$ is bounded constructible by [lem-sfb-coefficient-heart-lisse-extension-constructible]. The complex $Rj'_{*,A}K$ is bounded constructible by [lem-sfb-rational-open-direct-image-constructible], so the proper comparisons proved in steps 3--7 apply both to $(p,Rj'_{*,A}K)$ and $(q,K)$. The normal-crossings boundary comparison [lem-sfb-continuous-algcl-tame-boundary-comparison] applies to the actual $K$, including its inner extension by zero, and gives invertibility of $\beta_{j',K}$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent proof of geometric norm-coefficient projection, using independent proper finiteness and tame-boundary inputs.

proof.text: The equality $jq=pj'$ gives $Rj_*Rq_*\cong Rp_*Rj'_*$ in each coefficient category by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition]. Along this equality, the coefficient projection for the composite equals the two successive projections, by the counit-compatible composition of [lem-sfb-ringed-derived-monoidal-comparisons] and [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting]. The $p,j'$ route is invertible by step 9. In the $j,q$ route the $q$ projection is invertible, so cancellation proves $\beta_{j,G}$ invertible for this generator. All comparisons use the canonical inverse-image/tensor maps, so this is the specified transformation of step 8. Finite thick generation and step 8 now give invertibility of $\beta_{j,C}$ for every bounded constructible $A_U$-complex $C$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent proof of geometric norm-coefficient projection, using independent proper finiteness and tame-boundary inputs.

proof.text: Apply [sk-thm-nagata-compactification] to $t:T\to\operatorname{Spec}K$. Obtain $T\xrightarrow{j}\overline T\xrightarrow{p}\operatorname{Spec}K$ with $j$ a quasi-compact open and $p$ proper, all still separated of finite type over $K$. For the $Q$ of step 1, $Rj_{*,A}Q$ is bounded constructible by [lem-sfb-rational-open-direct-image-constructible]. Step 10 gives the $j$ comparison and steps 3--7 give the $p$ comparison on that object. Derived composition and the same counit-pasting equations identify their invertible composite with $\beta_{t,Q}$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent proof of geometric norm-coefficient projection, using independent proper finiteness and tame-boundary inputs.

proof.text: For the separably closed $K$, [lem-sfb-field-action-derived-section-transport] has trivial Galois group. Its exact equivalence identifies the module derived category over $\operatorname{Spec}K$ with the condensed coefficient module category, and $Rt_*$ with $Rp_{T*}$; it preserves scalar extension, units, counits and their coefficient projections. Consequently step 11 is precisely the stated $\pi_Q$, including the K-flat formula $q\mapsto1\otimes q$. For empty $T$ or $S$, or $L_0=0$, $Q=0$ and both functors give zero; all comparisons above are their unique isomorphism on zero. No step used an arithmetic action, completion, a finite-subextension-valued replacement of $B$, or flatness of $A\to B$.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-NC-e8ba33bf3 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item's 12 steps, the 3 new statement-only nodes, the statement of every cited node, main-20261015 direct-images proof paragraph (3), and HRS §3 Ex 3.1 and Lemma 4.1. The route (proper image, then qc-open image through tame-pair generators and the tame-boundary comparison, then Nagata compactification) follows paragraph (3). The proof is correctly marked agent and makes no SGA use. Proper step: the proper constructibility of det-sf-comp-continuous-algcl-finiteness, with PadicAlgCl identified with Ω by an isometric algebraic-closure isomorphism. Postcomposition by continuous E-endomorphisms of Ω is A-linear on B, and e=λ0(-)·1 splits A off B exactly. Countable-module reconstruction gives Ω⊗eH≅H with θ_v=m_v e, i.e. the fibre of β. The target is shown bounded before bounded conservativity is applied. Open step: β_jq=Rj_*β_q∘β_j by mate pasting and cancellation; I checked the retract inverse both ways. Step 12: field-action transport with trivial G. My own graph traversal finds no cycle and no ancestor cited; the ancestor proper/open scalar comparisons are not used. New nodes are true. Orthogonal basis: best approximation by local compactness plus ultrametric orthogonality. Reconstruction: H=IH via an uncountable almost-disjoint family; rank-one surjectivity; injectivity by μ_i. Geometric fibres: w-contractible point, C(π0U,F) matrices, continuous inversion, stratum recollement. Duplicate searches (orthogonal/ultrametric basis, rank-one/Morita, geometric-point detection) found only non-duplicates. Batch-5 flags are all generic: topos inverse-image exactness, a geometric-morphism definition, the pd module-category comparison, irreducible-separable derivative algebra, an SNC-boundary definition, and pushpull normalization. None is a trace-formula or Poincaré-duality step. The cross-unit generic tools in the split report are accepted. Maintainer note: steps 3-10 prove in general the statements of this item's ancestors lem-sfb-continuous-algcl-proper-/open-scalar-comparison, so their routes could be shortened; this is not a fault.
